Home.heroNote: The demo runs without signing up: a complete value stream with five processes, inventory and calculated metrics. Change one cycle time and watch the lead time respond.

Home.modulesTitle: Two modules under one roof — and more are coming
Home.modulesBody: Your lines show up in two places: as a process box in the value stream, and as a standalone planning unit in the capacity analysis. Both views run on the same master data and work independently of each other.
Home.modulesVsmBody: Current and future state, Rother & Shook symbology, every metric with its own visible arithmetic.
Home.modulesCapacityBody: A 12-month view per line, an automatic traffic light from the load rate, and a built-in recommendation — from cutting changeover times to outsourcing.
Home.modulesTeaser: More modules for the company overview are in the works.
Home.kpisTitle: Every number shows its own arithmetic
Home.kpisBody: Under each metric sits the formula with the values actually used. A surprising number therefore explains itself from its own inputs, instead of looking like a defect.

Home.checksBody: A value stream can be methodologically wrong and still look fine. The method check runs on every change and ranks by severity: first what invalidates a metric, then what only affects the drawing.
Home.checksLinkText: See every check in the demo →

checks.title: Capacity shortfall
checks.body: If the line cannot meet customer demand, inventory grows without bound. Little’s Law no longer holds, and the tool says exactly that instead of claiming a lead time.

checks.title: Push upstream of the pacemaker
checks.body: Everything upstream of the pacemaker needs a pull system. Where a connection still runs as push, it is named and counted.

checks.title: No pacemaker set
checks.body: Without a pacemaker, the ERP schedules every process individually. The map shows it that way, and the note explains why that is rarely intended.

Home.comparisonTitle: From current state to business case
Home.comparisonBody: Each future-state scenario is its own copy of the value stream. The comparison places them side by side and translates the lean metrics into the language budgets are decided in.
Home.comparisonNote: Example values, shown to illustrate the columns.
Home.comparisonLinkText: Set up your own scenario for free →

OgImage.headline: Value stream mapping with live calculation
OgImage.subline: Drawn to Rother/Shook — lead time, takt time and process cycle efficiency calculate along.

leadTime.definition: The time a part takes from the first to the last process step — including all waiting and buffer time in between, not just the processing itself.

cycleTimeSum.definition: The sum of the pure cycle times of every process in the chain — excluding the waiting time sitting in inventory between them.

pce.definition: Value-added time divided by lead time, as a percentage. Shows how much of the total lead time is actually value-adding rather than waiting in inventory. The rating follows rule-of-thumb figures from the lean literature for discrete manufacturing — below roughly 5 % is the unimproved norm, continuous flow starts around 25 %. Guide values, not a standard.

taktTime.definition: Available production time divided by customer demand. The pace at which one part must be finished for demand to be met — not a measured processing value, but a target.

availableMinutesPerDay.definition: How many minutes per day are actually produced (e.g. one 8-hour shift = 480 min, two shifts = 960 min, less breaks). The other factor in the takt time formula alongside customer demand.

exitRate.definition: How many parts per day actually leave the value stream. Set by the slowest process (bottleneck / time trap) after its OEE losses: available production time ÷ bottleneck cycle time. Not to be confused with customer demand, which sets takt time — output is measured, takt is required. Together with WIP it gives the lead time: PLT = WIP ÷ output.

balanceChart.definition: One bar per station whose height shows its load including OEE losses, with takt time as a horizontal line. Unlike the timeline below the value stream, the axis here is the station rather than the sequence — which is what makes it readable which station breaks takt and where work content could be moved.

capacityCoverage.definition: Actual output divided by customer demand. Below 100 % the line cannot meet demand: inventory then grows continuously, and lead time is no longer a stable figure but rises with every day.

processCycleTime.definition: The time a single process step takes to work on one part.

changeoverTime.definition: The time to switch a machine or process from one product or variant to the next.

oee.definition: Overall equipment effectiveness: the product of availability, performance and quality. Shows how much of the theoretically possible time is actually used in a value-adding way.

operatorCount.definition: How many people are needed to run this process step.

pacemaker.definition: The one process in the chain that sets the pace for the whole production — usually the last one before shipping. Production control schedules only here; every upstream process replenishes by pull.

wip.definition: Inventory of unfinished parts between two process steps. Together with daily demand it determines how long a part waits at this point.

bufferType.definition: How inventory between two processes is controlled: standard (uncontrolled), supermarket (pull — replenished only on withdrawal), FIFO lane (fixed sequence, limited capacity) or continuous flow (no buffer, the part moves straight on).

flowStyle.definition: How material flow is drawn: push (standard forwarding), pull (withdrawal from a supermarket), or shipment (delivery to/from supplier and customer). "Automatic" derives it from the inventory type.

kanbanType.definition: Only relevant with a supermarket: a production kanban triggers replenishment at the supplying process, a withdrawal kanban only triggers the transport of an already produced part.

supermarket.definition: A controlled buffer stock from which the downstream process withdraws exactly what it needs via kanban — the upstream process only replaces what was withdrawn.

fifo.definition: A first-in-first-out connection between two processes with no free withdrawal — the processing sequence is strictly preserved, usually with limited capacity.

onePieceFlow.definition: Parts flow one at a time and without an intermediate buffer directly from one process to the next — no waiting, no inventory between the steps.

bottleneck.definition: A process whose effective cycle time (cycle time ÷ OEE) exceeds takt time — in its current state it cannot serve customer demand.

heijunka.definition: Production mix and volume are spread evenly over time instead of running in large batches — it hangs off the pacemaker, because that is where production is actually scheduled.

pitch.definition: A fixed time increment (a multiple of takt time) in which the pacemaker produces and releases a consistent quantity — it makes production control work in manageable portions rather than piece by piece.

kaizenBlitz.definition: A concrete improvement point marked at a process, needed to get from the current to the future state — not a general improvement wish, but a targeted note at exactly this spot.

pieceValue.definition: What one piece of inventory is worth — usually the production cost up to this point, not the sales price. This single factor is all that is missing to turn a count on the shelf into an amount of money.

tiedUpCapital.definition: Inventory times value per piece: the money sitting in the value stream instead of in the bank. Halve the inventory in a scenario and half of it comes back — that is the figure an investment rests on.

supermarketSizing.definition: How many pieces a supermarket has to hold: cycle stock (replenishment interval × ADU) plus safety stock (covers variation) plus PLT stock (covers demand during production). Switching from push to pull replaces the stock that simply grew there with this calculated figure.

adu.definition: The average daily usage of this part at this point, in pieces per day. Not the same as the project's annual demand, which describes what the customer takes at the end of the stream. Read the ADU from a usage extract over a representative period.

aduStdDev.definition: How far daily usage swings around its mean, in pieces per day. It sets the safety stock. The calculator in the buffer panel works it out together with the ADU from a pasted series of daily usage figures.

plt.definition: The process lead time in days, measured on the value stream. Sizing a supermarket counts the lead time without the share this buffer itself contributes — otherwise its own size would feed into its own precondition.

cama.definition: The capacity traffic light for each line and month: does the available capacity cover demand? Uses the same figures as above on the process (cycle time, NEE — the same number as OEE), plus a shift model and monthly demand. Green is ok, orange/red means action needed, blue means underutilised.

loadRate.definition: Demand ÷ available capacity of a line in one month. Below 0.5 underutilised, up to 1.0 ok, up to 1.2 watch, above that overloaded — the basis of the CAMA traffic light.

CapacityGuide.metaDescription: Step by step: create lines, calculate monthly capacity, read the traffic light, and compare the forecast against actual hours worked.
CapacityGuide.title: Capacity management (CAMA) — step by step
CapacityGuide.intro: Capacity management is a standalone module: a line exists independently of whether a value stream is ever drawn for it. This guide walks through the full path, from the first line to comparing forecast against actual work.

steps.title: Create a line
steps.body: A workstation or production line, e.g. "Turning" — organization-wide, under capacity management, not tied to a single project.

steps.title: Enter master data
steps.body: Cycle time (minutes per piece), operator count, OEE (%), and shift model (1/2/3-shift) — the same figures as a VSM process box, but maintained independently of it here.

steps.title: Enter monthly demand
steps.body: Twelve values, one field per month. Optionally add a stress test (e.g. demand × 1.2) for an upside scenario.

steps.title: Read the traffic light
steps.body: Load rate = demand ÷ capacity, calculated automatically per month. Blue/green/orange/red show how tight the line is — the recommended action matches the color automatically.

steps.title: Add actual hours
steps.body: Once a month is closed: how many hours this line actually worked — in hours, not pieces, because a line can serve several product variants with different cycle times.

steps.title: Compare forecast vs. actual
steps.body: The line's chart shows required hours from the demand forecast, available hours from the shift model, and the actual hours entered, side by side — making it visible whether a year is tracking to plan.

steps.title: Track actions
steps.body: For each line: description, owner, due date, and optionally a target month — typically created as soon as a traffic light turns orange or red.

CapacityGuide.ctaBody: Capacity management is part of every Taktane account, whether or not a value stream exists yet.

DataSheet.intro: Take it to the line, fill it in, then enter it in Taktane. One row per station, in the order the part passes through them.
DataSheet.seoIntro1: This data sheet for value stream mapping travels to the line with you: one row per process step, using the same measurement instructions Taktane itself relies on.
DataSheet.seoIntro2: Once filled in, you enter the numbers into a project — Taktane then calculates lead time, takt time and process cycle efficiency live.
DataSheet.seoDemoLinkPrefix: Prefer trying the notation on screen first? The
DataSheet.seoDemoLinkSuffix: has the same value stream already filled in.
DataSheet.frameTitle: Frame data (applies to the whole chain)
DataSheet.howCycleTime: Cycle time: the time one piece actually takes at this station — timed part to part, without the waiting before or after. Not the time for a whole batch.
DataSheet.howChangeover: Changeover: from the last good part of the old variant to the first good part of the new one. Enter 0 where there is no changeover.
DataSheet.howOee: OEE: the share of planned time in which the station really produces good parts. From the machine report, otherwise estimated — entering 100 % means “no losses known”.
DataSheet.howOperators: Operators: how many people work at this station at the same time.
DataSheet.howWip: Inventory after: everything waiting behind this station for the next one — on pallets, on racks, in the buffer store. Count it, do not estimate: this number drives the lead time.

Pricing.metaDescription: Map and calculate a complete value stream for free, with one scenario and a PDF. What the higher plans add is in the table.
Pricing.title: Plans
Pricing.body: The free plan is not a guided tour with the doors locked: one complete value stream, one scenario calculated against it, the result as a PDF. What sits above differs in breadth — how many value streams, how many colleagues, how many scenarios.
Pricing.priceAnchor: A facilitated value stream workshop with external guidance costs a multiple of a year's subscription. The tool doesn't replace the facilitation — but the two days afterward, spent recalculating the numbers in Excel.
Pricing.tierFREEBody: One value stream, one scenario, two seats. Every metric, every method check, PDF export.
Pricing.tierSTARTERBody: Five value streams, three scenarios each, five seats. Plus importing process steps from a CSV.
Pricing.tierPROFESSIONALBody: Fifty value streams, unlimited scenarios, 25 seats. Including the industry benchmark.
Pricing.tierENTERPRISEBody: No volume limits, for several plants.
Pricing.comparisonBody: These numbers are not just printed here: they are the same limits the application checks against when you create something.

faq.question: What does the free plan cost?
faq.answer: Nothing. It covers one complete value stream with one future-state scenario, two seats and the PDF export. No credit card is asked for.

faq.question: Do I need to install anything?
faq.answer: No. Taktane runs in the browser. For recording data on the line there is also a printable data sheet.

faq.question: Can I take the result with me?
faq.answer: Yes. PDF export is included in every plan, the free one as well — the result of a workshop is the sheet that ends up on the wall afterwards.

faq.question: Can I try it first?
faq.answer: Yes, without signing up: the demo contains a value stream you can actually edit. Nothing is stored.

faq.question: What happens when I hit a limit?
faq.answer: Existing value streams stay untouched and readable. Only creating further ones is blocked, until you delete one or change the plan.

faq.question: How do I change plan?
faq.answer: You can subscribe to Starter and Professional directly, no request needed — the button on this page takes you to Stripe and back. Enterprise still runs through a request to us. The change applies to the organisation, not to individual accounts — every colleague in it gets it at the same time.

faq.question: How do I cancel?
faq.answer: Via “Manage subscription” in the dashboard — that opens Stripe's customer portal, where you can cancel, view invoices and update your payment method. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid period; the plan stays active until then.

Pricing.contactBody: Tell us how many value streams and how many colleagues — you get a price back, not a brochure.

Datenschutz.title: Privacy policy
Datenschutz.intro: This policy describes which personal data Taktane processes, for what purpose, and who it is shared with.
Datenschutz.controllerBody: The controller responsible for data processing is Tizian Seibert, trading as "Taktane by Seibert" (sole proprietorship), Rastenhoschet 7, 8752 Näfels, Switzerland, hallo@taktane.com. Full provider details are in the legal notice.
Datenschutz.dataBody: Account data: e-mail address and, when signing in via Google, the basic details Google provides (name, e-mail, profile picture). Project data: the value stream and process data you enter in the tool. Billing data: the plan you purchased and a customer reference at Stripe — payment card data itself is processed exclusively by Stripe, not by Taktane. Contact data: name, e-mail, company, job title, phone and message when you use the contact form, including the wording of any consent given. Attribution data: which campaign or search led to a visit (see "Cookies" below). Technical data: standard log data from the hosting infrastructure (e.g. IP address, timestamp, requested address) for security and troubleshooting.
Datenschutz.purposeBody: We process this data to provide the account and the purchased functionality, to bill subscriptions, to respond to contact-form enquiries, to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing activities, to prevent abuse, and to meet statutory obligations, in particular in bookkeeping.
Datenschutz.legalBasisBody: Processing in Switzerland is governed by the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP), based on good faith, proportionality and purpose limitation. Where data subjects reside in the EU, we additionally rely on the GDPR: performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)), consent (Art. 6(1)(a), e.g. for the contact form), or legitimate interest in a functioning and secure operation (Art. 6(1)(f)).
Datenschutz.processorsBody: Taktane uses the following service providers, which process data on our behalf: Supabase (database, authentication, file storage) — the database runs in the EU, specifically in Frankfurt am Main, Germany (region eu-central-1); Vercel Inc. (hosting the website and application) — the application also runs in Frankfurt am Main (region fra1); Stripe (payment processing and invoicing for paid plans); and Google LLC (optional sign-in via "Sign in with Google"). Stripe and Google may process data outside Switzerland and the EU, in particular in the USA, and are contractually bound to an adequate level of data protection (standard contractual clauses or the providers' own data processing agreements). For the value stream and process data an organisation enters itself, Taktane acts as that organisation's processor rather than as controller — we provide a data processing agreement (DPA) on request.
Datenschutz.cookiesBody: Taktane uses no cookies for third-party advertising or analytics. Necessary and set without consent: Supabase session cookies (keep you signed in), "NEXT_LOCALE" (remembers your chosen language), and "vsm_consent" (stores your decision on this cookie banner, valid 180 days). The one cookie that is not necessary is "vsm_attr": it records which campaign or search a visit first came from (only the details present in the requested address, e.g. utm_source), is readable server-side only, and expires after 30 days. For that cookie we ask for your consent via the banner at the bottom of the screen beforehand; you can decline or withdraw it at any time without affecting Taktane's functionality.
Datenschutz.retentionBody: Account data is kept until the account is deleted. Billing data is retained in line with statutory bookkeeping retention duties (generally ten years). Lead data is kept until its purpose no longer applies or deletion is requested. The attribution cookie expires automatically after 30 days, the consent decision after 180 days.
Datenschutz.rightsBody: You have the right to access the data processed about you, to have it corrected, deleted or its processing restricted, to receive it in a common format, and to withdraw any consent given at any time. Contact hallo@taktane.com for any of these. You may also contact the competent supervisory authority — in Switzerland the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), or within the EU the authority responsible for your place of residence.
Datenschutz.securityBody: Data is transmitted encrypted (TLS). Access to stored data is restricted at the database level (row level security) to the people and organisations authorised for it. Passwords are stored hashed by our authentication provider; Taktane itself never sees them in plain text.
Datenschutz.changesBody: We update this privacy policy whenever the processing or the legal situation changes. The current version is always available at this address.
Datenschutz.contactBody: For privacy-related questions, reach us at hallo@taktane.com.
